unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9-LEVEL: B1.1 - THEME 7: LIFE IN THE WORLD & NATURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students prepare a self-recording (visual, audio) at school/ at home, conducting an interview with classmates about ''endangered animals and their habitats and living conditions including where and how they live today and in the past, and ways to protect them from extinction'' and present it to the class and receiving feedback about it. They write and design the content of a documentary film script and then they present and apply it as a film-showing event in class by inviting other students as protectors, activists, or people who give harm to endangered animals. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme is based on the concept of ''endangered animals and their habitats and living conditions including where and how they live today and in the past, and ways to protect them from extinction'' in English. As they are upper secondary students in Year 9, they are expected to know what an endangered animal is, what a habitat is, what protection is in their own language. They are also aware that almost all people, although there are exceptions, would know different types of animals, different types of endangered animals, why they are endangered and what should be done to protect them. Students can think about and express such situations in their own languages, but they may not know how to say them in a foreign language if they have not been covered at all or only partially covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language would prepare them to identify the same concepts later and help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information about the new concept and theme more easily in their foreign language, English. In terms of preparation for the current new theme, it is assumed that they have learnt basic animals as pets and marine animals such as ''cats, dogs, rabbits, fish, dolphins, cows, sheep, ducks, hens, turtles etc.'', animal habitats such as ''rivers, mountains, seas, ponds, farms etc.'', how to ask what animals are, what they eat, where they live such as ''What’s/is it/this? It’s/is a cow.? What does it eat? It eats grass. Where does it live? It lives on a farm'', to explain whether animals exist in a particular habitat such as ''There’s/is a cow on the farm. There are fish in the sea. They live in the sea'' in English from the previous themes or years. These language items and vocabulary can be used as a basis for learning the new language grammar items in use in the current theme, making the new ones in the current theme easier to learn.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is expected that the physical, cognitive, affective, and social factors are appropriate and suitable for students to learn about ''endangered animals and their habitats and living conditions including where and how they live today and in the past, and ways to protect them from extinction''. Knowledge of ''endangered animals and their habitats and living conditions including where and how they live today and in the past, and ways to protect them from extinction'' in this theme. Therefore, a contextual written story about animals for remembering and practising the previously learnt items could be delivered to students to discuss and fill in the blanks with the required words in pairs. This session can help them revise all vocabulary and grammatical items in use from previous themes or previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how much these items are used correctly to be able to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise or practise for revising the previous knowledge and to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammar items in use in the current theme.
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about endangered animals and conservation efforts in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Digital Role-Play: Save an Endangered Animal Students work in small groups and choose or are assigned an endangered animal (e.g., (Antalya) Caretta caretta turtles or Anatolian leopards). Using a web tool, they create a digital character or visual story that introduces the animal, its habitat, and the problems it faces (such as pollution or habitat loss). The animal ''speaks'' using recorded audio or text-to-speech to describe its challenges and suggest solutions. Groups present their digital work to the class while others take notes and give feedback on vocabulary, fluency, and presentation skills. After all presentations, the class holds a brainstorming session to discuss ideas for protecting the animals, using phrases like ''Every little bit helps!'' and ''We need to act now!''. The teacher provides feedback on the presentations, and students finish with a clear plan of actions and solutions. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To identify endangered animals and conservation efforts in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Collaborative Reading Puzzle: Endangered Animals The teacher divides a complex reading text about endangered animals (e.g., caretta caretta turtles, Anatolian leopards) into sections, each with unique information (like habitat, threats, or solutions). Students work in small groups, and each group reads one section, identifying key points and preparing questions about missing information they need from other groups. After reading, groups take turns asking and answering questions to complete the full picture of the topic (e.g., ''What is threatening the Anatolian leopard?''). Once they gather all the information, each group presents a summary of their findings, combining what they read and learned from others. The class ends with a discussion on solutions to protect endangered animals. The teacher gives feedback on reading comprehension, vocabulary use, and collaboration throughout the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe endangered animals, their habitats, and ways to protect them from extinction in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Endangered Animal Habitat Matching Game The teacher provides students with two sets of cards: one set with endangered animals (e.g., polar bear, sea turtle) and another with habitats (e.g., ocean, rainforest). Students work in pairs to match the animals with their correct habitats (e.g., Polar bear-Arctic). Once matched, they create simple sentences following the models on the board, such as ''A polar bear lives in the ocean'' or ''A tiger lives in the jungle'', and practice saying them aloud to improve pronunciation. The pair that completes the matches and sentences correctly and the fastest wins the game. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To identify endangered animals and their habitats in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Endangered Animals Gap-Fill and Pronunciation Practice The teacher starts by providing a short reading or audio about endangered animals like (Antalya) Caretta caretta sea turtles or Anatolian leopards. Students learn about their habitats, challenges, and ways to protect them. Afterward, students use the Web 2.00 tool to complete a gap-fill exercise with sentences such as ''A Caretta caretta turtle lays eggs on the (Mediterranean coast)''. After completing the exercise, students read their sentences aloud to practise pronunciation. The teacher then provides feedback on their accuracy and fluency. The activity ends with a class discussion on protecting animals, using phrases like ''Every little bit helps!'' and ''It’s not too late to act!''. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
